content.text: No minimum-commitment, take-or-pay, volume-cap, or shortfall-penalty obligation binds the Issuer/Depositor anywhere in the agreement; the only fee we pay is usage-based. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Section 3.8 Servicer's Fees. As compensation for performing its obligations under this Agreement, the Servicer will be paid the Servicing Fee. On each Payment Date, the Issuer will pay the Servicing Fee to the Servicer according to Section 8.2 of the Indenture.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on us. Our only compensation obligation to Cellco is the Servicing Fee, payable solely "As compensation for performing its obligations under this Agreement" and calculated as "one-twelfth of the Servicing Fee Rate" (0.75%) times "the Adjusted Pool Balance" — i.e., a purely usage/asset-based fee for services actually rendered, with no floor, minimum, take-or-pay, or shortfall penalty. Likewise the Supplemental Servicing Fee and Temporarily Excluded Receivables Servicing Fee are computed on actual Recoveries and actual Principal Balances. Acquisitions of Additional Receivables (Sections 2.1(b) and 2.1(d)) are conditional transfers with no committed minimum volume or frequency, and no volume cap restricts us. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "volume", "take or pay" and "obligated to purchase" returned no obligation running against us. The two "shortfall" hits confirm the planner's read and run in our favour or against third parties: the Marketing Agent's Credit Payment deposit obligation on a "shortfall in Collections" (p0211) is a payment to us, and the requirement that "The customer is required to purchase a new qualifying device" (p0595) is an upgrade-offer condition on Obligors, not on the Issuer or Depositor. This sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for services actually performed), so no redline is warranted.
